shared_body: A communal biscuit tin has gone missing. We don’t share an office, so the list of suspects is everyone, in three countries. The enquiry begins today.
optional_prompt: Where was the tin last seen? The desk welcomes highly unreliable testimony.
private_body: Dear reader, this little compartment is yours for December. I measured it myself. It will take a letter, a song or roughly half a decent sandwich.

shared_body: Outside my window a man is attempting to straighten a string of lights by glaring at it. Wherever December has found you, in a coat or in sun cream, I hope the view contains something worth a second look.
optional_prompt: Send a sentence about one thing you can see or hear where you are.
private_body: Pick something in the distance and give it a moment of your undivided attention. The email will keep. Goodness knows the last six did.

shared_body: At 09.14 a reindeer entered reception wearing a visitor’s lanyard. Asked who he was here to see, he pointed at the ceiling. The first instalment of our rolling dispatch ends here, largely because the ceiling has requested representation.
optional_prompt: Sydney desk, fancy filing the next line? Cebu and UK can pick it up in the replies when convenient.
private_title: A cracker from the tree desk
private_body: What do you give a Christmas tree who has everything? Some space. Its relatives are coming and there are about six hundred of them.

shared_body: Our first exhibit is a mug bearing the words Dishwasher Safe. This claim has now survived considerably longer than the words. Admission to the museum is one raised eyebrow.
optional_prompt: Send a desk object and its entirely truthful museum label. A description is plenty.
private_body: Today’s award goes to whoever gives a file a name that makes sense six months later. One day a stranger will whisper your name over a folder and mean it kindly.

shared_body: Fair in the kitchen. Variable near the laundry. A deep depression over the chair where the clean clothes live. Conditions expected to improve when somebody wants the chair badly enough.
private_body: You have received a voucher for ten uninterrupted minutes of a thing you like. Valid indefinitely. The editor tried to put an expiry date on it and was overruled by the cat.

shared_body: FOR SALE. Artificial Christmas tree. Very realistic. Has dropped needles in the loft eleven months running. Buyer collects, preferably before it starts attracting theoretical squirrels.
private_body: Imagine a choir taking one magnificent breath, then realising the conductor has left his music on the bus. Enjoy the resulting silence.

shared_body: The editor located the end of the sticky tape on the first attempt. A civic reception seems excessive. A small plaque would do.
optional_prompt: What tiny victory would you like entered in the public record?
private_body: Think of one thing you quietly put right this week. Give yourself the credit for it now, while the minutes of the meeting are still open.

shared_body: A circular mark has been found on the editor’s desk. Experts agree it is consistent with the base of a biscuit tin, a mug, or a circle. We have thanked the experts and cancelled their second afternoon.
optional_prompt: Offer the enquiry an alternative explanation for the mark.
private_body: If your shoulders have quietly migrated towards your ears, invite them downstairs. There is more room and the rent is considerably lower.

shared_body: Picture the scene. A robin sits on a garden fork. Behind it, a gardener waits. Both appear to believe the other has made an appointment.
optional_prompt: Supply tomorrow’s headline in eight words or fewer.
private_body: There is a kindness in asking the question everyone else is still trying to phrase. Somewhere in a call, three muted colleagues are mouthing “thank you”.

shared_body: Today’s food critic has reviewed the lunch he ate over his keyboard. Notes of toasted bread, mature cheddar and the faint possibility of finding the letter G again.
optional_prompt: What food, smell or sound says December to you?
private_body: If circumstances permit, take the first bite somewhere the inbox cannot see you. The inbox has never once invited you round to its place.

shared_body: Somebody once wrote “I’ve done that bit already” at the bottom of a handover. Six ordinary words. A whole evening went back to its owner.
optional_prompt: Share a small kindness you remember. Ask before naming anyone.
private_body: Think of someone whose messages make your day easier. If you fancy it, send them one sentence saying why. “You always tell me which attachment to open” is practically a sonnet.

shared_body: A paper snowflake made from an old agenda has won our sculpture prize. Repeated folding has improved the agenda beyond recognition.
private_body: Choose a song you know well enough to join halfway through. The newsroom offers excellent seats and no opinion whatsoever on your high notes.

shared_body: Our festive houseplant has responded well to being moved six inches to the left. The editor has asked whether the same treatment might improve his writing. Trials continue.
private_body: Look closely at a leaf, a cloud or whatever is making shadows near you. For once there will be no follow-up question about its distance from a property.

shared_body: Our postal service spans three time zones and consists largely of a man checking the spelling of people’s names. The letters are the one part of this newspaper he is delighted to print exactly as received.
private_body: Some of the best things people say about us happen after we’ve left the call. Today this pigeonhole has room for one to find its way back.

shared_body: A witness heard a sound “broadly consistent with a custard cream”. On further questioning it emerged that several leading biscuits make no sound at all until eaten. The witness has requested crumbs immunity.
optional_prompt: What question should the enquiry put to its next witness?
private_body: Fetch a drink you actually want. If you find yesterday’s cup on the journey, kindly escort it home. Its family have been very brave.

shared_body: Our imaginary radio station needs a record for the interval between finishing a difficult task and discovering the next one. Current interval length is four seconds. We can extend it for a good chorus.
optional_prompt: Name a song and tell us when to play it. A link is welcome.
private_body: Which song would play over the opening credits of your working day? Hum the first bar. A considerable orchestra is available in your head and works for scale.

shared_body: The reindeer has returned his lanyard. He has also returned three other lanyards, a cupboard key and a flattering reference from Payroll. We may have to take him on permanently.
optional_prompt: Cebu desk, where does he go next? Pass the story to whichever desk wakes up with a good line.
private_body: Patience rarely gets a round of applause. It usually sounds like somebody saying “of course” and explaining the thing a second time. If that was you this year, take a bow.

shared_body: International post has landed. Parcels may contain music, moving pictures or an extremely specific compliment. Customs have waved everything through except a pun, which they are holding for questioning.
optional_prompt: If you joined the draw, visit your pigeonhole. Share a gift only if you fancy it and its sender is happy.
private_body: The gift the editor would send every household is a charging cable long enough to reach the comfortable chair. Until procurement agrees, please accept the comfortable chair in spirit.

shared_body: Yesterday’s report referred to a silent night. A reader with a young child, a nearby road and a neighbour assembling furniture invites us to visit. The correction is gladly made.
private_body: Why was the bauble so good at interviews? Years of hanging about looking interested while somebody else did all the talking.

shared_body: Clue of the day. Seven letters. Appears without warning and consumes the last free half-hour in your diary. Answer printed upside down in spirit only. MEETING.
private_body: A blank space has been reserved here for a thought of absolutely no commercial value. Mine is whether ducks enjoy rain or merely have excellent coats.

shared_body: The great pleasure of a handover is handing something to a person who is just starting their day and being told, “Go on, I’ve got it.” The pleasantest five words in international publishing.
optional_prompt: UK desk, start a final one-line dispatch. Leave our overseas desks something splendid to wake up to.
private_body: There’s a particular skill in knowing what the next person needs to know and giving it to them in two lines. The editor is especially grateful. He’s still trying to get this one down to three.

shared_body: An independent witness reports that the editor appears noticeably taller on video calls than he does in person. Asked if this could be relevant, he moved his camera and disconnected himself.
optional_prompt: Last theories before the enquiry presents its findings?
private_body: Pick a pen you enjoy writing with and put one good thing about today on paper. An especially good potato counts. The archive has accepted far less.

shared_body: We’re gathering the small things colleagues did for one another this year. Grand speeches may be left at reception. A plain sentence about a particular Tuesday goes straight to the front of the queue.
optional_prompt: May we print a moment from your year tomorrow? Tell us what happened and how to credit you. Check with anyone named.
private_body: Leave yourself one kind sentence to find when you next log in after a break. “Start with the little job, there’s tea” is sound management from somebody who knows the team.

shared_body: I lifted my laptop to pack it away. Underneath was the biscuit tin. It has been supporting my camera since March. To everyone who contributed evidence, and to the shortbread finger, who tried to help on day six and was eaten for its trouble, I owe an apology. To everyone who took a little weight off somebody else this year, very often without them seeing what was underneath: thank you. Back to the studio, Si.
private_body: Dear reader, wherever you open this and whoever is nearby, I hope there’s a moment in the coming days that feels entirely yours. It’s been lovely having you here. Si.
